title: Narmer Palette shows Egypt existed before reunification

tellings.quote: because the hallmark of the beginning of the dynastic period is known as the reunification of upper and lower Egypt as indicated by the Nar pallet or the meanis pallet.

plain: Egypt's first dynasties are said to begin with a "reunification of upper and lower Egypt," and the researcher Geoffrey Drumm tells Michels this is shown by the Narmer Palette, an ancient Egyptian carved stone slab he also calls the Menes palette. His point is that you can only reunite something that was united before, so an Egypt would have existed before its known history begins. His case rests on the word "reunification" as historians use it; what the slab itself shows, and whether it marks a first union or a second, he does not say.
